     4	/-!
     5	# Pauli basis test soundness interface
     6	
     7	This module contains the quantitative error function and the closed definitions
     8	used to state Pauli basis test soundness.  The carriers are concrete
     9	finite-dimensional vectors and matrices so that the soundness proof can use the
    10	existing Hilbert-space API without introducing a dependency cycle.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The interface supports blueprint
    15	`thm:pauli`, with paper origin
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    17	The distance functionals use blueprint `def:state-distance` and
    18	`def:povm-distance`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    31	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    32	as specified by blueprint `thm:pauli`,
    33	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    34	-/
    35	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    36	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    37	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    38	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    39	
    40	/-- Monotonicity obligation for adjusting the universal constants in
    41	`deltaQld` on the source parameter domain. This Lean-only helper supports the
    42	enlargement of `a` and shrinkage of `b` for `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1` recorded in
    43	`rem:pauli-robustness-form` and stated as `lem:delta-qld-mono-support`,
    44	blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex`; the source makes this constant adjustment
    45	at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1402`. It is
    46	not an additional hypothesis of `thm:pauli` or `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    47	theorem deltaQld_mono {P : AdmissibleParams} {a a' b b' ε : ℝ}
    48	    (ha0 : 1 ≤ a) (ha : a ≤ a') (hb : b' ≤ b) (hb' : 0 < b')
    49	    (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) :
    50	    deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ≤ deltaQld a' b' ε P.m P.d P.q := by
    51	  have hmd : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) :=
    52	    Nat.one_le_cast.mpr (Nat.mul_pos P.one_le_m P.hd)
    53	  have hmd0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) := by linarith
    54	  have hq : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (P.q : ℝ) := by
    55	    obtain ⟨k, -, hk⟩ := P.hq
    56	    rw [hk]
    57	    exact_mod_cast Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by norm_num)
    58	  unfold deltaQld
    59	  simp only [Real.rpow_eq_pow]
    60	  have h1 : ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ a ≤ ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ a' :=
    61	    Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hmd ha
    62	  have h2 : ε ^ b ≤ ε ^ b' := Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge' hε0 hε1 hb'.le hb
    63	  have h3 : (P.q : ℝ) ^ (-b) ≤ (P.q : ℝ) ^ (-b') :=
    64	    Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hq (neg_le_neg hb)
    65	  have h4 : (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b * ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ))) ≤
    66	      (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b' * ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ))) :=
    67	    Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le (by norm_num)
    68	      (neg_le_neg (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hb hmd0))
    69	  have hsum : 0 ≤ ε ^ b + (P.q : ℝ) ^ (-b) +
    70	      (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b * ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ))) := by
    71	    have := Real.rpow_nonneg hε0 b
    72	    have := Real.rpow_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg P.q) (-b)
    73	    have := Real.rpow_nonneg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)
    74	      (-(b * ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ)))
    75	    linarith
    76	  exact mul_le_mul (mul_le_mul ha h1 (Real.rpow_nonneg hmd0 a) (by linarith))
    77	    (add_le_add (add_le_add h2 h3) h4) hsum
    78	    (mul_nonneg (by linarith) (Real.rpow_nonneg hmd0 a'))
    79	
    80	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    81	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from blueprint
    82	`def:EPR`; paper
    83	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    84	-/
    85	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    86	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    87	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    88	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    89	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    90	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
    91	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    92	    (fun p =>
    93	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
    94	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
    95	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
    96	
    97	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
    98	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
    99	in blueprint `thm:pauli`; paper
   100	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
   101	-/
   102	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   103	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   104	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   105	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   106	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   107	  fun p q =>
   108	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
   109	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
   110	    else 0
   111	
   112	/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from blueprint
   113	`thm:pauli`, paper origin
   114	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   115	-/
   116	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   117	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   118	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   119	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   120	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   121	  fun p q =>
   122	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
   123	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
   124	    else 0
   125	
   126	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in blueprint
   127	`thm:pauli`, paper origin
   128	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   129	-/
   130	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   131	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   132	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   133	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   134	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   135	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   136	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   137	  fun p q =>
   138	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   139	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   140	    else 0
   141	
   142	/-- Lift a conjugated B-side effect to the full ideal register in blueprint
   143	`thm:pauli`, paper origin
   144	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   145	-/
   146	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   147	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   148	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   149	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   150	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   151	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   152	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   153	  fun p q =>
   154	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   155	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   156	    else 0

   158	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   159	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   160	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   161	`thm:pauli`, paper origin
   162	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   163	-/
   164	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   165	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   166	  ιA' : Type
   167	  ιB' : Type
   168	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   169	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   170	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   171	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   172	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   173	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   174	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   175	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   176	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   177	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1

    65	\section{Key theorem forms}
    66	
    67	Throughout, $q = 2^r$ with $r$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple
    68	$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \ge 1$ and $m \mid q$, and
    69	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
    70	over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four
    71	theorem forms.
    72	\begin{enumerate}
    73	  \item \textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There
    74	  is a function $\delta_S(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,
    75	  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every
    76	  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test
    77	  succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, there is a projective
    78	  measurement $\{\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in
    79	  $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\delta_S$-consistent, on
    80	  average over a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$ and in both bases
    81	  $W \in \{X,Z\}$, with the corresponding points measurements
    82	  $\{\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$ of the strategy, together with the
    83	  symmetric counterpart of this relation.
    84	  \item \textbf{Missing instantiation obligation.}  The classical low
    85	  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)$ is well
    86	  defined, and the combined point and line measurements assembled in the
    87	  analysis constitute a strategy for it of value at least
    88	  $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$.  The game's question distribution draws
    89	  its axis and diagonal indices through an index function
    90	  $\chi_{2m+2}\colon \F_q \to \{1,\ldots,2m+2\}$ with classes of equal size
    91	  $q/(2m+2)$, so the game exists only when $2m+2$ divides $q$.

    93	  form under the additional hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$.  Among

   102	  admissible $q$, with no divisibility hypothesis: the question

   122	\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}
   123	
   124	We examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical
   125	low-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression
   126	paper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,
   127	arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
   128	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
   129	\footnote{Tracked in \localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source
   130	consulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at
   131	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   132	lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
   133	line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization
   134	with its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its
   135	proof, and admissibility are at
   136	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   137	lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}
   138	There, the combined point measurements
   139	$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
   140	$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
   141	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
   142	individual degree game with parameters
   143	\[
   144	  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
   145	  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
   146	\]
   147	of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
   148	for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
   149	The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution
   150	over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
   151	
   152	The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
   153	admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
   154	incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
   155	in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
   156	$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
   157	$\chi(s)$ with
   158	\[
   159	  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
   160	  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
   161	\]
   162	so that the $m'$ classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\F_q$ into sets of equal
   163	size $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \nmid q$ neither the index
   164	function nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.
   165	
   166	Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
   167	is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
   168	$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
   169	divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
   170	admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is
   171	undefined for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$: for instance
   172	$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs
   173	the instantiation without addressing the divisibility.  Thus even before the
   174	two soundness-import obligations below are considered, this route can apply to

   177	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   178	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   179	
   180	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   181	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   182	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   183	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   184	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   185	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   186	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   187	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   188	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   189	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
   190	the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
   191	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   192	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
   193	open for the printed tensor-code route. Both obligations are independent of
   194	the divisibility question and remain open for that route at every dimension
   195	where that game is defined.  They would also arise from an attempt to prove
   196	soundness of the directly indexed game by the same tensor-code import.  The
   197	established proof for the directly indexed game takes a different route through
   198	the low individual degree theorem and therefore bypasses both obligations.
   199	
   200	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   201	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   202	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
   203	measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
   204	three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
   205	subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
   206	test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
   207	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
   208	direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
   209	send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
   210	$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
   211	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
   212	last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly
   213	in $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to
   214	one prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to
   215	the other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \emph{Synchronicity
   216	test}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered
   217	pair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their
   218	answers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this
   219	test with probability $1-\eps$ together with an integer parameter
   220	$K \ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code
   221	--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and
   222	distance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements
   223	$\{G_c\}$ and $\{\tilde G_c\}$ with outcomes in $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$,
   224	consistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's
   225	lines measurements, and with each other, up to
   226	$\eta'(m',t,K,\eps,n^{-1}) = \mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \cdot
   227	\mathrm{poly}(\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.
   228	
   229	\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}
   230	The source asserts that the $\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$
   231	is this test.  It is not, in four respects.
   232	(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals
   233	two points of a \emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent
   234	--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line
   235	question reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$
   236	polynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the
   237	diagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$
   238	and $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and
   239	both directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line
   240	description carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of
   241	the pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the
   242	compatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the
   243	\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the
   244	\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The
   245	construction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the
   246	hidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.
   247	(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \in \F_q$; the test's carry
   248	only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class
   249	$\chi^{-1}(i)$.  For the comparison with the directly indexed game, this
   250	dependence is now retained in a correlated residue register rather than
   251	averaged away, as explained below.  That construction resolves this part of
   252	the direct-game transport, but it has not been composed with the distinct
   253	pair-question construction required for the tensor-code test.
   254	(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$
   255	in the test against $2/9$ in the game.  Once the per-branch predicates are
   256	matched, the intended bookkeeping bound is that the constructed strategy's
   257	rejection probability in the test is at most $\tfrac32$ times the game's
   258	rejection probability, up to the $O(1/(m'q))$ of item~(iv); this bound is
   259	the target of the obligation, not an established fact.
   260	(iv)~The game's predicate fixes an acceptance convention on diagonal
   261	questions with zero direction --- an event of probability at most
   262	$2/(m'q)$, recorded in the blueprint's remark on zero directions --- for
   263	which the test has no counterpart branch.
   264	Finally, the displayed conclusions of Theorem~4.7 pair one prover's points
   265	measurements with the other prover's tensor-codeword measurement, and the
   266	first prover's tensor-codeword measurement with the second prover's lines
   267	measurements, while the game-level statement asserts the point consistency
   268	in both directions; deriving the stated form uses the role symmetrization
   269	of the test and belongs to the correspondence.  None of these steps is
   270	difficult to state, but none is carried out in the source, and together
   271	they replace the asserted one-line identity by a reduction carrying its
   272	own value bound.
   273	
   274	\paragraph{Obligation 2: the parameter bound.}
   275	Theorem~4.7 requires $K \ge 12 m' t = 12 m' (d+1)$.  The source
   276	instantiates $K = (m')^3 d$, which meets the bound iff
   277	$(m')^2 d \ge 12(d+1)$: this holds for all $d \ge 1$ when $m' \ge 5$,
   278	holds at $m' = 4$ exactly when $d \ge 3$, and fails for every $d$ when
   279	$m' \le 3$.  In the game's parameter domain the dimension divides the
   280	admissible field size and is therefore a power of two, so the source's
   281	instantiation violates the hypothesis exactly at $m' \in \{1,2\}$ for
   282	every $d$ and at $m' = 4$ for $d \in \{1,2\}$ --- in particular, in the
   283	multilinear regime $d = 1$, at every dimension $m' \le 4$.  A candidate
   284	repair is to instantiate $K = \max((m')^3 d,\, 12 m'(d+1))$; the open
   285	obligation is then to re-absorb the error, that is, to check that
   286	$\mathrm{poly}(m',t,K)$ and $e^{-K/(m')^2}$ still collapse to the form
   287	$a(dm')^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bm'd})$ in the small-$m'$ cases where the
   288	maximum is $12m'(d+1)$ --- plausible, since there
   289	$e^{-K/(m')^2} = e^{-12(d+1)/m'}$ decays in $d$ at a rate comparable to
   290	$2^{-m'd}$ for $m' \le 4$, but not checked here.
   291	
   292	In the correspondence of Obligation~1, the only role of the divisibility
   293	$m' \mid q$ is to make the $\chi$-sampled index uniform.  The underlying
   294	mathematics does not need the divisibility.  The low
   295	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} samples its axis
   296	index $i$ uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly, with no index function
   297	on $\F_q$ and no divisibility hypothesis,%
   298	\footnote{See the test figure in \path{references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex}.}
   299	and the tensor-code test is likewise a test about the code
   300	$\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$, not about an encoding of indices into $\F_q$.  The
   301	$\chi$-based packaging exists so that the question distribution is
   302	conditionally linear, which the introspection machinery requires for the
   303	game the players actually play --- the Pauli basis test at dimension $m$,
   304	where admissibility does supply the divisibility.  The game at dimension
   305	$2m+2$ never appears in a verifier; it is an internal analysis device in the
   306	proof of the polynomial-pair lemma, so nothing there requires its question
   307	distribution to be conditionally linear.
   308	
   309	\section{Repairs and current status}
   310	
   311	\paragraph{Direct index sampling (soundness established).}
   312	For arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the formalization defines the line-point
   313	distribution over $\F_q^{m'}$ by sampling the point, the axis index
   314	$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
   315	$i-1$ coordinates directly.  In the resulting game, line questions carry
   316	the index $i$ (and, for diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place
   317	of the seed $s \in \F_q$.  Soundness form~4 is established for this game
   318	through the low individual degree theorem and the general-simultaneity
   319	combining reduction analysed in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich}.

    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The extraction proof contains two
    23	  incorrect numerical steps and later suppresses the range projection when
    24	  passing from unitary conjugation to isometry conjugation.

    40	\section{Key theorem forms}
    41	
    42	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    43	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    44	\[
    45	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    46	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    47	\]
    48	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    49	\[
    50	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    51	  \qquad
    52	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    53	\]
    54	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    55	\[
    56	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    57	\]
    58	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    59	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    60	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    61	
    62	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    63	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    64	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    65	\[
    66	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    67	\]
    68	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    69	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    70	$\Delta$.

    72	\section{Numerical defects in the source proof}
    73	
    74	Lines~1715--1742 of
    75	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    76	construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
    77	estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
    78	$\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
    79	source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
    80	\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
    81	small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
    82	$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
    83	
    84	The triangle inequality yields
    85	\[
    86	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
    87	\]
    88	so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
    89	$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
    90	$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
    91	universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
    92	vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
    93	are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.

    95	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    96	
    97	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    98	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    99	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
   100	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
   101	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   102	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   103	
   104	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   105	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   106	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   107	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   108	\[
   109	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   110	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   111	\]
   112	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   113	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   114	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   115	
   116	The finite-dimensional estimate is proved in
   117	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/RangeProjection.lean}. For a complete POVM
   118	$\{N_h\}$, an orthogonal projection $Q$, and $Q\vartheta=\vartheta$, it gives
   119	\[
   120	  \sum_h\|(N_hQ-T_h)\Delta\|^2
   121	  \le 2\sum_h\|(N_h-T_h)\Delta\|^2+2\|\Delta-\vartheta\|^2.
   122	\]
   123	The proof uses $\sum_h N_h^\dagger N_h\le I$, so it also applies when the
   124	measurement is not projective. The same module proves the isometry form under
   125	the exact identity $N_h\phi=\phi M_h$ and its two bipartite placements. The
   126	unit-ancilla embedding and its composition with a unitary, including the
   127	identity $U(M\ot I\ot I)U^\dagger\phi=\phi M$, are proved in
   128	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/Ancilla.lean} for $\phi=UJ$,
   129	$J\psi=\psi\ot\eta$, $\|\eta\|=1$, and $U^\dagger U=I$.
   130	
   131	The supplied-data transfer is proved in
   132	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/StateTransfer.lean} and
   133	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/OperatorTransfer.lean}. Given an actual
   134	\path{ExtractionWitness}, the local maps adjoin a normalized EPR state and
   135	apply its swap unitaries. Register reassociation identifies their tensor
   136	action with the witness's transformed state, so its squared distance from
   137	the ideal state is at most $\delta$. The existing swapped total-Pauli POVMs
   138	intertwine with these maps; the two bipartite range-projection estimates
   139	bound each full squared operator-family sum by $4\delta$. Thus the same
   140	\path{PauliSoundnessWitness} satisfies all three soundness estimates at
   141	$\max\{\sqrt\delta,4\delta\}$. This is an auxiliary result with supplied
   142	extraction data, not a new bridge field or a proof of soundness for arbitrary
   143	strategies.

    36	\section{Key theorem forms}
    37	
    38	Theorem \path{thm:pauli} compares, for each $W\in\{X,Z\}$ and
    39	$u\in\F_q^M$, the effect $A^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_u$ or
    40	$B^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_u$ directly with the corresponding ideal Pauli
    41	projector.  The same raw prescribed-answer effects occur in
    42	\path{cor:pauli-binary} of \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}.%
    43	\footnote{See
    44	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
    45	lines~1426--1487, and the closing proof in
    46	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
    47	lines~1862--1876.}
    48	
    49	\section{Formal representation discrepancy}
    50	
    51	The formal game has one sum-type answer alphabet for all question types.
    52	Earlier soundness declarations first postprocessed a Pauli-question
    53	measurement by sending every malformed answer to the register value zero.
    54	For $u\ne0$ this completed effect equals the raw effect attached to
    55	\texttt{pauliOutcome $u$}.  At zero it is instead
    56	\[
    57	  M^{\mathrm{completed}}_0
    58	  = M_{\texttt{pauliOutcome }0}+M_{\mathrm{malformed}}.
    59	\]
    60	Consequently the old headline distance compared the completed family, not the
    61	raw family in the paper.  Rejection of malformed answers did not make
    62	$M_{\mathrm{malformed}}$ identically zero, so this was not a definitional
    63	identification.
    64	
    65	\section{Repair}
    66	
    67	For Alice, rejection on the oriented Pauli-to-point edge bounds the state
    68	mass of $M_{\mathrm{malformed}}$ by
    69	$|\mathrm{PauliEdge}|\,\varepsilon$.  The reverse point-to-Pauli edge gives
    70	the same bound for Bob.  If the transported strategy state is within
    71	$\delta$ of the ideal state, contractivity gives
    72	\[
    73	  \|\widetilde M_{\mathrm{malformed}}\ket{\mathrm{ideal}}\|^2
    74	  \leq 2\delta^2+2|\mathrm{PauliEdge}|\,\varepsilon.
    75	\]
    76	Since completion changes only outcome zero, the squared triangle inequality
    77	then yields, for each player,
    78	\[
    79	  d_{\mathrm{raw}}
    80	  \leq 2d_{\mathrm{completed}}+4\delta^2
    81	      +4|\mathrm{PauliEdge}|\,\varepsilon.
    82	\]
    83	On $0\leq\varepsilon\leq1$, the soundness function dominates
    84	$\varepsilon$; the existing scalar absorption estimates therefore absorb all
    85	three terms by enlarging only the existential prefactor $a$.  The usual
    86	monotonicity argument covers $\varepsilon>1$.
    87	
    88	The declarations
    89	\leanid{raw\_pauli\_operator\_distanceA\_le\_completed} and
    90	\leanid{raw\_pauli\_operator\_distanceB\_le\_completed} implement the two
    91	transfer estimates, and
    92	\leanid{exists\_arbitrary\_strategy\_raw\_isometry\_bounds} performs the
    93	scalar absorption.  The public theorems \leanid{pauli\_soundness} and
    94	\leanid{pauli\_soundness\_qubit} now use the raw effects directly.  The
    95	completed-family distances remain as internal support for extraction and
    96	Naimark dilation.
    97	
    98	\section{Conclusion}
    99	
   100	The paper statement is unchanged and requires no additional hypothesis.  The
   101	formalization now proves its raw-effect conclusion for both players with the
   102	printed form of $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$.  The discrepancy and repair are
   103	tracked by \ghissue{665}; documentation follow-up is tracked by

For `u ≠ 0` this completed effect is the raw prescribed-answer effect; at zero it is the raw effect plus the total malformed-answer effect. Before PR #668 the public distance used the completed family. The current source-facing distances use the raw effects directly, while the completed family remains internal support. |
docs/DEVIATIONS.md:381:| **Why** | Rejection of malformed answers bounds their state mass but does not make their effects definitionally zero. The proof therefore bounds malformed-answer mass on the two oriented Pauli–point edges, transfers the completed-family estimates to the raw family, and absorbs the added linear and squared errors into the existential prefactor of `deltaQld`. |

  1836		&  \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \notag \\
  1837		&\approx_{md/q}  \E_u \sum_{\substack{h, h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-8} \\
  1838		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1839		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes V_\bob  \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-9}
  1840		\end{align}
  1841		where the equality in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9} follows from the identity in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-6}, and the approximation in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-8} follows from the following calculation:
  1842		\begin{align*}
  1843			& \E_u \sum_{\substack{h \neq h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \\
  1844			&= \sum_{h \neq h'} \left( \E_u \mathbf{1}[g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)] \right) \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \\
  1845			&\leq \frac{md}{q}\;.
  1846		\end{align*}

  1851			\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}} &\approx_{O(\delta_S^{1/4})} \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1852			&\geq 1 - O(\delta_S^{1/2})\;,
  1853		\end{align*}
  1854	        where the last line comes from \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-5}.

  1856		\[
  1857		\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}} \leq O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)\;.	
  1858		\]

  1862	We now prove \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. 
  1863	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}]
  1864		Let $\strategy = (\psi,M)$ be a projective strategy for $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\alice \bob$. As mentioned at the beginning of \Cref{sec:commutation}, we assume that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is padded with sufficiently many ancilla $\ket{0}$ qubits. Let $\phi_\alice$ be the following isometry mapping the register $\alice$ to the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ where $\alice'$ and $\alice''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$:
  1865		\[
  1866			\phi_\alice: \ket{\theta}_\alice \mapsto V_\alice (\ket{\theta}_\alice \otimes (\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice' \alice''})
  1867		\]
  1868		where $V_\alice$ is the unitary acting on $\alice \alice' \alice''$ from \Cref{lem:qld-unitary}. Define the isometry $\phi_\bob$ analogously. \Cref{lem:qld-unitary} then implies that there exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1869		\[
  1870			\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld
  1871		\]
  1872		and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1873		\[
  1874			\phi_\alice \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\alice \, \phi_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \phi_\bob \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\bob \, \phi_\bob^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1875		\]
  1876		where the $\approx$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. This shows that $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ is a self-test for the strategy $\strategy^\pauli$ with robustness $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. We conclude the proof by making the identification of registers $\alice \alice'$ with $\alice'$ and $\bob \bob'$ with $\bob'$ to be consistent with the statement of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. We also note that, when unpacking the dependence on parameters $\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for some universal constants $a > 1, 0 < b < 1$, as desired.
  1877	\end{proof}

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	r"""Model-free completion gate for a formalization track.
     3	
     4	``local/protocols/completion.md`` defines when a track may be declared
     5	finished.  This script decides the mechanically checkable part of that
     6	definition: it runs no model, opens no network connection, and uses only the
     7	standard library, so its verdict is reproducible by anyone holding the commit.
     8	
     9	Seven criteria, in the protocol's numbering:
    10	
    11	* ``C1`` proof integrity — no ``sorry``/``admit`` site, project ``axiom``
    12	  declaration, native evaluation or ``trustCompiler`` under the track's Lean
    13	  root.
    14	* ``C2`` headline axioms — a committed ``AxiomAudit`` file covering every
    15	  headline theorem (the axiom *values* come from the CI build: delegated).
    16	* ``C3`` paper-gap register — every row terminal.
    17	* ``C4`` blueprint — every ``\lean{}`` node marked ``\leanok`` or exempted.
    18	* ``C5`` comparator — challenge recorded, the *registered* expected copy
    19	  present and naming every headline theorem, verified library commit an
    20	  ancestor-or-equal of the commit being declared.
    21	* ``C6`` docs truthful — no stale nonzero open-site claim once ``C1`` holds.
    22	* ``C7`` artifact readiness — every file an ITP artifact submission needs is
    23	  committed (the snapshot build and its leak scan are delegated).
    24	
    25	``C2``, ``C4``, ``C5`` and ``C7`` each have a half this gate cannot decide
    26	without running something — the axiom values, ``blueprint_leanok_axioms.py
    27	--ci``, the comparator drift regeneration and the artifact snapshot's leak
    28	scan.  When their static half holds they report ``DELEGATED`` rather than
    29	``PASS``, so a completion comment can never quote a ``PASS`` for a check nobody
    30	ran; ``DELEGATED`` does not count against the exit code, and a failing static
    31	half is still ``FAIL``.
    32	
    33	Shared rules, never restated here:
    34	
    35	* the sorry-site rule is parsed out of
    36	  ``results/telemetry/owner-tools/estimate.sh`` (``SORRY_SITE_RE``).  The POSIX
    37	  character classes of that ERE are translated to Python syntax; the alternation
    38	  itself is used verbatim, so the estimate posted on the tracker issue and this
    39	  gate can never disagree about what a site is.
    40	* explicit ``axiom``/``constant`` declarations are found with ``DECL_RE`` of
    41	  ``scripts/audit_lean_axiom_declarations.py``, and comments are stripped with
    42	  that module's ``strip_lean_comments``.  Comment stripping there is strictly
    43	  stronger than the estimate's ``sed 's/--.*$//'`` (it also blanks block
    44	  comments and string literals), so the gate can only ever drop sites that are
    45	  not real; it never invents one.
    46	* the set of blueprint environments a node may live in is read out of
    47	  ``_TEX_ENV_BEGIN_RE`` of ``scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py`` — the parser
    48	  behind ``scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py`` — so ``C4`` and the blueprint
    49	  tooling can never disagree about what a node is.
    50	
    51	Exit codes: 0 every mechanically checkable criterion passed, 1 at least one
    52	failed, 2 the gate could not run (missing shared rule, unknown track).

     5	/-!
     6	# Non-vacuity of the Pauli basis test soundness theorem
     7	
     8	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` is an implication: for every admissible
     9	parameter tuple `P`, every `ε ≥ 0` and every strategy `S` for
    10	`pauliBasisTest P` with `1 - ε ≤ S.value`, extraction data exist whose three
    11	error quantities are bounded by `deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q`.  A reader is
    12	entitled to ask two questions about such a statement, and this module answers
    13	both with citable declarations.  Nothing here changes or restates an existing
    14	definition or theorem; every result is a corollary of material already on the
    15	main development.
    16	
    17	## Q1 — are the hypotheses satisfiable?
    18	
    19	`AdmissibleParams` is inhabited (`nonVacuousParams`, and hence
    20	`nonempty_admissibleParams`), and for *every* admissible `P` the honest
    21	strategy of `lem:pauli-completeness` is a strategy for `pauliBasisTest P`
    22	itself with value exactly `1` (`exists_pauliBasisTest_strategy_value_one`);
    23	the symmetric presentation used by `exists_spcc_value_one` has
    24	`pauliBasisTest P` as its underlying game definitionally
    25	(`pauliBasisTestSymm_toGame`).  Consequently the hypothesis triple
    26	`0 ≤ ε`, `S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)`, `1 - ε ≤ S.value` is jointly
    27	satisfiable — with `ε = 0`, the strongest case
    28	(`pauli_soundness_hypotheses_satisfiable`) — and `pauli_soundness` applied to
    29	it yields an unconditional statement
    30	(`pauli_soundness_applies_to_honest_strategy`).
    31	
    32	## Q2 — is the conclusion non-trivial?
    33	
    34	The bound is `deltaQld a b ε m d q = a * (m*d)^a * (ε^b + q^(-b) + 2^(-b*m*d))`
    35	with `a, b` existentially quantified by the theorem, so no *single* numeric
    36	value can be extracted.  What can be shown, and is shown here, is that
    37	whatever the constants `a ≥ 1` and `0 < b < 1` produced by `pauli_soundness`
    38	are, the bound is not vacuously large: along the explicit admissible family
    39	`nonVacuousParams n` the error at `ε = 0` tends to `0`
    40	(`tendsto_deltaQld_nonVacuousParams`), so for every `η > 0` there are
    41	admissible parameters at which the soundness conclusion bounds all three
    42	distances by less than `η` (`exists_admissibleParams_deltaQld_lt` and the
    43	combined `pauli_soundness_nontrivial`).
    44	
    45	**What is *not* shown.** This is a statement about the `ε = 0` section of
    46	`deltaQld` for a *chosen* parameter family, not a uniform rate: it does not
    47	locate a threshold `ε₀ > 0` below which the bound is small for a *fixed*
    48	parameter tuple, and it does not compare `deltaQld` against the trivial bound
    49	on `rawPauliOperatorDistanceA`/`rawPauliOperatorDistanceB` at fixed
    50	parameters. It also does not assert anything about the numerical size of the
    51	constants `a` and `b`, which the source theorem leaves implicit
    52	(`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    53	Continuity of `deltaQld` in `ε` at `0` is recorded separately
    54	(`tendsto_deltaQld_eps_zero`) so that a reader can see that the `ε = 0`
    55	section is the limiting case of the `ε > 0` statement rather than a
    56	degenerate one.
    57	
    58	## References
    59	
    60	Supports blueprint `thm:pauli` and `lem:pauli-completeness`; paper origin
    61	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`
    62	and `:1229-1421`.  This module is formalization-only bookkeeping: it states no
    63	new mathematics of the source and introduces no hypothesis.
    64	-/

    77	/-! ### Q1: the hypotheses of `pauli_soundness` are satisfiable -/
    78	
    79	/-- An explicit admissible parameter family: field size `q = 2^(2n+1)`,
    80	ambient dimension `m = 1` and degree `d = n + 1`.  Admissibility is immediate —
    81	`2n+1` is odd, `1 ∣ q`, and `1 ≤ n + 1` — so `AdmissibleParams` is inhabited
    82	and, since `m * d = n + 1` and `q` both grow with `n`, the family is also the
    83	one used for the quantitative statements below.  Formalization-only: it is a
    84	witness, not a constraint added to `def:admissible`. -/
    85	def nonVacuousParams (n : ℕ) : AdmissibleParams where
    86	  q := 2 ^ (2 * n + 1)
    87	  m := 1
    88	  d := n + 1
    89	  hd := Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n)
    90	  hq := ⟨2 * n + 1, ⟨n, by ring⟩, rfl⟩
    91	  hdvd := one_dvd _

   104	/-- Every admissible Pauli basis test has a strategy of value one *for the game
   105	`pauliBasisTest P` itself*.  This is `exists_spcc_value_one` transported along
   106	`pauliBasisTestSymm_toGame`, which holds definitionally; it is the form in
   107	which the hypothesis `1 - ε ≤ S.value` of `thm:pauli` is met.  Blueprint
   108	`lem:pauli-completeness`, paper
   109	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1229-1421`. -/
   110	theorem exists_pauliBasisTest_strategy_value_one (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   111	    ∃ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), S.value = 1 := by
   112	  obtain ⟨S, -, hS⟩ := exists_spcc_value_one P
   113	  exact ⟨S.toStrategy, hS⟩
   114	
   115	/-- The hypotheses of `thm:pauli` are jointly satisfiable, and satisfiable in
   116	the strongest case `ε = 0`: there are admissible parameters carrying a strategy
   117	whose value is `1`, so `1 - ε ≤ S.value` holds for every `ε ≥ 0`. -/

   119	    ∃ (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)),
   120	      ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 ≤ ε → 1 - ε ≤ S.value := by
   121	  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := exists_pauliBasisTest_strategy_value_one (nonVacuousParams 0)
   122	  refine ⟨nonVacuousParams 0, S, fun ε hε => ?_⟩
   123	  rw [hS]
   124	  linarith

   126	/-- `thm:pauli` applied to hypotheses that are actually met: for the constants
   127	it produces, *every* admissible parameter tuple carries a value-one strategy
   128	for which the extraction data and the three error bounds exist at `ε = 0`.
   129	The statement is unconditional — there is no hypothesis left for a reader to
   130	doubt. -/
   131	theorem pauli_soundness_applies_to_honest_strategy :
   132	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   133	      ∀ P : AdmissibleParams, ∃ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), S.value = 1 ∧
   134	        ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   135	          ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
   136	              deltaQld a b 0 P.m P.d P.q ∧
   137	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   138	              rawPauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b 0 P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   139	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   140	              rawPauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b 0 P.m P.d P.q) := by
   141	  obtain ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hb1, hmain⟩ := pauli_soundness
   142	  refine ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hb1, fun P => ?_⟩
   143	  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := exists_pauliBasisTest_strategy_value_one P
   144	  refine ⟨S, hS, hmain P 0 le_rfl S ?_⟩
   145	  rw [hS]
   146	  norm_num

   148	/-! ### Q2: the error function is genuinely small in an explicit regime -/
   149	
   150	/-- Formalization-only arithmetic: a negative real power of a power of two,
   151	rewritten as an inverse integer power of `2^b`.  Used to put both `q`-dependent
   152	and `md`-dependent summands of `deltaQld` on the same geometric scale. -/
   153	private theorem two_pow_rpow_neg (b : ℝ) (M : ℕ) :
   154	    ((2 ^ M : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-b) = (((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ M)⁻¹ := by
   155	  have hcast : ((2 ^ M : ℕ) : ℝ) = (2 : ℝ) ^ (M : ℝ) := by
   156	    rw [Real.rpow_natCast]
   157	    push_cast
   158	    ring
   159	  rw [hcast, ← Real.rpow_mul (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2),
   160	    ← Real.rpow_natCast ((2 : ℝ) ^ b) M,
   161	    ← Real.rpow_mul (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2),
   162	    ← Real.rpow_neg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)]
   163	  congr 1
   164	  ring
   165	
   166	/-- Formalization-only arithmetic: the `2^(-b*md)` summand of `deltaQld` as an
   167	inverse integer power of `2^b`. -/
   168	private theorem two_rpow_neg_mul_natCast (b : ℝ) (M : ℕ) :
   169	    (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b * (M : ℝ))) = (((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ M)⁻¹ := by
   170	  rw [← Real.rpow_natCast ((2 : ℝ) ^ b) M,
   171	    ← Real.rpow_mul (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2),
   172	    ← Real.rpow_neg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)]
   173	
   174	/-- The error at `ε = 0` along the explicit family, bounded by a
   175	polynomial-over-geometric expression.  Formalization-only: the bound is a
   176	convenience for the limit below, not a statement of the source. -/
   177	private theorem deltaQld_nonVacuousParams_le (a b : ℝ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 0 < b) (n : ℕ) :
   178	    deltaQld a b 0 (nonVacuousParams n).m (nonVacuousParams n).d (nonVacuousParams n).q ≤
   179	      2 * a * (((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ ⌈a⌉₊ / ((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (n + 1)) := by
   180	  have ht1 : (1 : ℝ) < (2 : ℝ) ^ b :=
   181	    Real.one_lt_rpow_iff_of_pos (by norm_num) |>.mpr (Or.inl ⟨by norm_num, hb⟩)
   182	  have ht0 : (0 : ℝ) < (2 : ℝ) ^ b := lt_trans zero_lt_one ht1
   183	  have hmd : ((nonVacuousParams n).m * (nonVacuousParams n).d : ℕ) = n + 1 := by
   184	    simp
   185	  have ha0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ a := le_trans zero_le_one ha
   186	  -- the three summands of the error bracket
   187	  have hzero : (0 : ℝ) ^ b = 0 := Real.zero_rpow (ne_of_gt hb)
   188	  have hq : (((nonVacuousParams n).q : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-b) = (((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (2 * n + 1))⁻¹ := by
   189	    rw [nonVacuousParams_q]
   190	    exact two_pow_rpow_neg b (2 * n + 1)
   191	  have hexp : (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b * ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))) = (((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (n + 1))⁻¹ :=
   192	    two_rpow_neg_mul_natCast b (n + 1)
   193	  -- geometric comparison: the `q` summand is the smaller one
   194	  have hpow : ((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (n + 1) ≤ ((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (2 * n + 1) :=
   195	    pow_le_pow_right₀ ht1.le (by omega)
   196	  have hinv : (((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (2 * n + 1))⁻¹ ≤ (((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (n + 1))⁻¹ :=
   197	    one_div_le_one_div_of_le (pow_pos ht0 _) hpow |>.trans_eq (by rw [one_div])
   198	      |>.trans_eq' (by rw [one_div])
   199	  have hinvpos : (0 : ℝ) < (((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (n + 1))⁻¹ := inv_pos.mpr (pow_pos ht0 _)
   200	  -- the prefactor
   201	  have hbase : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) := by
   202	    exact_mod_cast Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.succ_ne_zero n)
   203	  have hceil : a ≤ (⌈a⌉₊ : ℝ) := Nat.le_ceil a
   204	  have hpre : ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ a ≤ ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ ⌈a⌉₊ := by
   205	    rw [← Real.rpow_natCast (((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) ⌈a⌉₊]
   206	    exact Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le hbase hceil
   207	  have hprenn : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ a := Real.rpow_nonneg (by linarith) a
   208	  unfold deltaQld
   209	  simp only [Real.rpow_eq_pow]
   210	  rw [hmd, hzero, hq, hexp, zero_add]
   211	  have hstep : (((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (2 * n + 1))⁻¹ + (((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (n + 1))⁻¹ ≤
   212	      2 * (((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (n + 1))⁻¹ := by linarith
   213	  calc a * ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ a *
   214	        ((((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (2 * n + 1))⁻¹ + (((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (n + 1))⁻¹)
   215	      ≤ a * ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ ⌈a⌉₊ * (2 * (((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (n + 1))⁻¹) :=
   216	        mul_le_mul (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hpre ha0) hstep
   217	          (add_nonneg (inv_nonneg.mpr (pow_nonneg ht0.le _))
   218	            (inv_nonneg.mpr (pow_nonneg ht0.le _)))
   219	          (mul_nonneg ha0 (pow_nonneg (by linarith) _))
   220	    _ = 2 * a * (((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ ⌈a⌉₊ / ((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (n + 1)) := by
   221	        rw [div_eq_mul_inv]
   222	        ring

   241	    hbase.comp (tendsto_add_atTop_nat 1)

   243	      2 * a * (((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ ⌈a⌉₊ / ((2 : ℝ) ^ b) ^ (n + 1))) atTop (𝓝 0) := by

   250	admissible parameters at which the soundness error at `ε = 0` is below any
   251	prescribed `η > 0`; in particular below `1`, and so below any trivial bound. -/
   252	theorem exists_admissibleParams_deltaQld_lt (a b : ℝ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 0 < b)
   253	    {η : ℝ} (hη : 0 < η) :
   254	    ∃ P : AdmissibleParams, deltaQld a b 0 P.m P.d P.q < η := by
   255	  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ :=
   256	    ((tendsto_deltaQld_nonVacuousParams a b ha hb).eventually

   263	theorem tendsto_deltaQld_eps_zero (a b : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) (m d q : ℕ) :

   266	    ((Real.continuousAt_rpow_const 0 b (Or.inr hb.le)).continuousWithinAt).tendsto
   267	  unfold deltaQld
   268	  exact ((hrpow.add tendsto_const_nhds).add tendsto_const_nhds).const_mul _
   269	
   270	/-- **Q1 and Q2 together.** For the constants produced by `thm:pauli` and any
   271	`η > 0` there are admissible parameters carrying a value-one strategy — so the
   272	hypotheses hold — for which the theorem's conclusion bounds the state distance

   277	theorem pauli_soundness_nontrivial :
   278	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   279	      ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∃ (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)),
   280	        S.value = 1 ∧ deltaQld a b 0 P.m P.d P.q < η ∧
   281	        ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   282	          ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ <  η ∧
   283	            (∀ W : PauliKind, rawPauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W < η) ∧
   284	            (∀ W : PauliKind, rawPauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W < η) := by
   285	  obtain ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hb1, hmain⟩ := pauli_soundness
   286	  refine ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hb1, fun η hη => ?_⟩
   287	  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ :=
   288	    ((tendsto_deltaQld_nonVacuousParams a b ha hb).eventually
   289	      (eventually_lt_nhds hη)).exists
   290	  set P := nonVacuousParams n with hP
   291	  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := exists_pauliBasisTest_strategy_value_one P
   292	  obtain ⟨w, hstate, hA, hB⟩ := hmain P 0 le_rfl S (by rw [hS]; norm_num)

   294	    fun W => lt_of_le_of_lt (hA W) hn, fun W => lt_of_le_of_lt (hB W) hn⟩

    36	it adds the total effect of malformed answers. -/
    37	theorem completedPauliEffect_eq_raw_add_wrongForm {P : AdmissibleParams} {ι : Type*}
    38	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : Measurement (PauliAnswer P) ι)
    39	    (W : PauliKind) (u : PauliRegister P) :
    40	    (M.postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u =
    41	      M.effect (.pauliOutcome u) +
    42	        if u = 0 then ProjectiveSetting.wrongFormEffect (.pauli W) M else 0 := by
    43	  classical
    44	  rw [Measurement.postprocess_effect, ProjectiveSetting.wrongFormEffect,
    45	    Finset.sum_filter]
    46	  by_cases hu : u = 0
    47	  · subst u
    48	    simp only [ite_true]
    49	    calc
    50	      (∑ answer, if pauliAnswerOrZero answer = 0 then M.effect answer else 0) =

    52	            (if validPauliAnswer (.pauli W) answer = false then M.effect answer else 0)) := by
    53	        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    54	        intro answer _
    55	        cases answer <;> simp [pauliAnswerOrZero, validPauliAnswer]

    58	        congr 1

    62	    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (.pauliOutcome u)]

     1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.SoundnessDefs
     2	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree.RejectionBounds
     3	
     4	/-!
     5	# Extending Pauli soundness bounds from `ε ≤ 1` to the full error domain
     6	
     7	The Pauli basis test soundness statement quantifies over every error parameter
     8	`0 ≤ ε`, while the extraction and isometry arguments that establish it are
     9	carried out for `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`.  This module supplies the two Lean-only facts that
    10	bridge the two domains.
    11	
    12	## Main results
    13	
    14	* `deltaQld_mono_epsilon` — the error scale `deltaQld` is monotone in `ε`
    15	  on `0 ≤ ε`; only the `ε ^ b` summand depends on `ε`.
    16	* `pauli_isometry_bounds_extend_epsilon` — the soundness conclusion for every
    17	  `ε` in `[0, 1]` implies the same conclusion for every `0 ≤ ε`, at the same
    18	  universal constants `a` and `b`.
    19	
    20	For `1 ≤ ε` the success hypothesis `1 - ε ≤ S.value` carries no information:
    21	it already follows from `Strategy.value_nonneg` applied at `ε = 1`.  The
    22	`ε ≤ 1` result is therefore instantiated at `ε = 1` and its conclusion pushed
    23	up to the larger `ε` by monotonicity of `deltaQld`.  No trivial witness and no
    24	uniform numeric bound are involved.
    25	
    26	## References
    27	
    28	These are formalization-only support results for blueprint `thm:pauli`, whose
    29	statement is at paper
    30	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`
    31	and whose isometry step is proved at
    32	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1862-1876`.  The
    33	source states the theorem for every `ε ≥ 0` and argues the substantive case
    34	`ε ≤ 1`; the reduction recorded here is the bookkeeping that the source leaves
    35	implicit.  It adds no hypothesis to `thm:pauli` and changes no constant.
    36	-/
    37	
    38	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    39	
    40	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    41	
    42	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    43	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    44	
    45	noncomputable section
    46	
    47	/-- The Pauli-test error scale `deltaQld` is monotone in the error parameter `ε`
    48	on `0 ≤ ε`.  Only the summand `ε ^ b` depends on `ε`, and the prefactor
    49	`a * (m * d) ^ a` is nonnegative, so the bound follows from monotonicity of
    50	`Real.rpow` in its base.
    51	
    52	Unlike `deltaQld_mono`, which adjusts the universal constants `a` and `b` and is
    53	therefore restricted to `ε ≤ 1`, this lemma keeps `a` and `b` fixed and holds on
    54	the whole domain `0 ≤ ε` of blueprint `thm:pauli`, paper
    55	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`. -/
    56	theorem deltaQld_mono_epsilon {P : AdmissibleParams} {a b ε ε' : ℝ}
    57	    (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 0 < b) (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hle : ε ≤ ε') :
    58	    deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ≤ deltaQld a b ε' P.m P.d P.q := by
    59	  have hmd : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) :=
    60	    Nat.one_le_cast.mpr (Nat.mul_pos P.one_le_m P.hd)
    61	  have hmd0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) := by linarith
    62	  unfold deltaQld
    63	  simp only [Real.rpow_eq_pow]
    64	  have hεb : ε ^ b ≤ ε' ^ b := Real.rpow_le_rpow hε0 hle hb.le
    65	  have hpre : 0 ≤ a * ((P.m * P.d : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ a :=
    66	    mul_nonneg (by linarith) (Real.rpow_nonneg hmd0 a)
    67	  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (by linarith) hpre
    68	
    69	/-- Domain extension for the Pauli basis test soundness bounds: if the state and
    70	operator estimates hold at fixed constants `a`, `b` for every error parameter in
    71	`[0, 1]`, then they hold for every `0 ≤ ε`.
    72	
    73	For `1 < ε` the hypothesis `1 - ε ≤ S.value` is weaker than the hypothesis at
    74	`ε = 1`, which is `0 ≤ S.value` and holds for every strategy
    75	(`Strategy.value_nonneg`).  The witness produced at `ε = 1` therefore serves at
    76	`ε`, and its three bounds are pushed up by `deltaQld_mono_epsilon`.
    77	
    78	This lemma is a Lean-only bridge between the domain of blueprint `thm:pauli`
    79	(paper
    80	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`,
    81	which assumes only `ε ≥ 0`) and the domain on which the isometry argument at
    82	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1862-1876` is
    83	carried out.  It mentions no unproved declaration and weakens nothing: the
    84	conclusion is the source conclusion at the source's own `ε`.
    85	
    86	A caller holding the `[0, 1]` result with the constants packaged existentially
    87	destructures that existential first and applies this lemma to the resulting
    88	`a`, `b`:
    89	
    90	```
    91	obtain ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hb1, hbounds⟩ := (the `[0, 1]` result)
    92	exact ⟨a, b, ha, hb, hb1, pauli_isometry_bounds_extend_epsilon ha hb hbounds⟩
    93	```
    94	
    95	The existentially packaged form is deliberately not provided as a lemma of its
    96	own: its hypothesis would be an inline existential matching the conclusion, the
    97	proof-evasion pattern that `scripts/audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py`
    98	(issue #493) exists to catch.  Keeping the constants explicit makes the domain
    99	restriction `ε ≤ 1` — the only difference between hypothesis and conclusion —
   100	visible in the binder structure. -/
   101	theorem pauli_isometry_bounds_extend_epsilon {a b : ℝ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 0 < b)
   102	    (h : ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε → ε ≤ 1 →
   103	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   104	          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   105	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
   106	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   107	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   108	              pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   109	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   110	              pauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q)) :
   111	    ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   112	      ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   113	        ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   114	          ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
   115	              deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   116	          (∀ W : PauliKind,
   117	            pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   118	          (∀ W : PauliKind,
   119	            pauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) := by
   120	  intro P ε hε S hS
   121	  rcases le_or_gt ε 1 with hle | hgt
   122	  · exact h P ε hε hle S hS
   123	  · obtain ⟨w, hstate, hA, hB⟩ :=
   124	      h P 1 zero_le_one le_rfl S (by simpa using S.value_nonneg)
   125	    have hmono : deltaQld a b 1 P.m P.d P.q ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q :=
   126	      deltaQld_mono_epsilon ha hb zero_le_one hgt.le
   127	    exact ⟨w, hstate.trans hmono, fun W => (hA W).trans hmono,
   128	      fun W => (hB W).trans hmono⟩
   129	
   130	end
   131	
   132	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+below repair ill-typed expressions; there is no well-formed universal proposition
